instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires periodic expense statements to be filed by registered principals (not lobbyists), indicating no separate lobbyist periodic spending report is required.
Expense statements are due twice yearly (July 31 and January 31), not annually.
The only periodic spending statement described is semiannual, not monthly.
The statute sets July 31 and January 31 filing dates, not quarterly deadlines.
Semiannual reporting is required of principals, but this chunk is for a lobbyist’s periodic spending report and the statute does not require such a lobbyist report.
No triannual filing cadence is stated; only semiannual principal expense statements are described.
The statute specifies a semiannual principal expense statement and does not provide any other cadence for a lobbyist periodic spending report.
The statute provides for principal expense statements rather than any lobbyist periodic spending report, so there is no lobbyist filing cadence.
Since the law imposes periodic expense-statement filing duties on principals rather than lobbyists, it does not require lobbyists to file a spending report even when there is no activity.
Aggregate total lobbying expenditures are reported in the principal’s expense statement, not in a lobbyist spending report required of the lobbyist.
Compensation to lobbyists is included in amounts principals report, but the statute does not require lobbyists themselves to file a periodic spending report containing total compensation.
The principal must list amounts paid to each lobbyist over $200, but there is no requirement for a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report breaking compensation down by payer.
The statute’s detailed content requirements apply to the principal’s expense statement, not to any lobbyist periodic spending report.
Daily itemization of time is required in a principal’s record, but the statute does not require a lobbyist to file an itemized spending report.
Expense categories are specified for the principal’s filing, not for a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
Office space, utilities, supplies, and employee compensation (overhead/indirect costs) are reported by principals in some cases, not by lobbyists in a required periodic spending report.

The expense statement must include reimbursements to officials authorized under §13.621(7)(a), but this is a principal reporting obligation rather than a lobbyist periodic spending report requirement.
Principals list a lobbyist’s name and address when payments exceed $200, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report including their contact information.
The statute requires registered principals to file the spending statement, so it does not impose on lobbyists a report that would include principal names.
No lobbyist-filed spending report is required, so the law does not require lobbyists to report principal contact information in such a report.
Nature/purpose of the principal is disclosed in the principal’s registration, not in a lobbyist periodic spending report.
Topics/issues must be reported by principals under §13.67, but there is no lobbyist periodic spending report requiring general issues.
Reasonably specific topic descriptions are required in the principal’s topic reporting regime, not in a lobbyist spending report.
Legislative proposal and rule numbers are reported by principals, but the statute does not require a lobbyist periodic spending report that includes bill/action identifiers.
Reporting of each legislative proposal or proposed administrative rule number is imposed on principals, not on lobbyists via a periodic spending report.
The principal must report identifiers and topics but the statute does not require stating a support/oppose position, and in any event this is not a lobbyist periodic spending report.
Principals estimate proportion of time spent per proposal/topic (not expenditures per issue), and there is no lobbyist periodic spending report requirement.
The principal’s record itemizes time including meetings with officials, but the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed spending report listing contacts made.

Reporting in §13.68 concerns reimbursements to specified officials/candidates, and while §13.625 addresses gifts to relatives/household members as an exception, nothing requires a lobbyist spending report to include household members of officials.

unscoreable_emissions.justification: Because no lobbyist periodic spending report is required and no alternate cadence is specified for lobbyists, there is no 'other' cadence to describe.
